combat_history.event: First flight of the Boeing Airpower Teaming System, later named MQ-28 Ghost Bat.
combat_history.significance: First Australian-designed-and-built combat aircraft in over 50 years.

modernization.description: Maturing autonomy, payloads and integration with crewed RAAF aircraft.
modernization.impact: Moves crewed-uncrewed teaming toward operational capability.

vulnerabilities.description: Still maturing; not yet an operational combat capability.
vulnerabilities.context: Autonomy and teaming are hard, evolving problems.

vulnerabilities.description: Depends on robust links and trustworthy autonomy in contested EW.

operational_patterns.typical_deployment: Scouting, electronic warfare, surveillance and risk-absorption ahead of crewed fighters across long Indo-Pacific distances.
operational_patterns.typical_task_group: Teamed with F-35A, Super Hornet and E-7 Wedgetail.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: The U.S. CCA effort pursues the same loyal-wingman concept at larger scale.
China's stealth UCAV is a penetrating strike drone; the Ghost Bat is a teaming aircraft.
peer_comparisons.video_angle: How the US-aligned and Chinese drones differ.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: The MQ-25 is a carrier tanker UAV; both reflect Boeing's uncrewed push.

doctrine.role: Loyal-wingman uncrewed combat aircraft teaming with crewed fighters to extend reach and survivability.
doctrine.employment: Several drones per crewed aircraft scout, jam, surveil and absorb risk in contested airspace.
doctrine.design_philosophy: Affordable, modular uncrewed mass to multiply crewed airpower over vast distances.
doctrine.threat_context: Australia's bid for the next phase of air warfare across the Indo-Pacific.
doctrine.comparison_frame: Read against the US CCA programme, China's GJ-11 and Boeing's MQ-25.
